name: discover-layer-sequences-full
description: The `sequences` layer's descriptor at `form: "full"` — the one form that carries the descriptor PROSE, asked for one layer at a time because the project-wide `full` discovery is REFUSED with `over-budget` on every project (`negative/discover-project-full-over-budget.json`), and the refusal's second step is exactly this request. Together the fifteen per-layer `full` vectors replay every layer, kind and field annotation the model contract ships, verbatim, which is where the shipped-prose oracle (`packages/tools/tests/test_model_contract_conformance.py`) rides: rewording an annotation in the contract is a protocol-output change, and this is the output it changes. Of this layer: the `sequence.steps` collection, the other `(swc, runnable)` composite. Compare it with the same descriptor inside `examples/discover-project-all-layers-present.json`, which is this document with every `description` dropped and the three descriptor booleans (`optional`, `required`, `immutable`) omitted where they are `false`.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` shape of a SWCraft project: fifteen scaffolded layers, `hardware/` among them. Nothing about the response depends on which elements are in the layer: the inventory is derived from the model contract through the registry, not from the files.

layers.description: Sequence scenarios, one task each; each is drawn as a sequence diagram whose files are named from the scenario's name.

element_kinds.description: One sequence scenario: an ordered walk through some of the runnables of exactly one task, drawn as a sequence diagram. The steps must follow the task's own runnable order.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The scenario's identity, which also names its sequence diagram's files. Must match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ — a rule of this layer alone, deliberately not the AUTOSAR `Identifier` rule.

fields.name: task
fields.description: The name of the declared task this scenario walks; exactly one per scenario, and every step must be mapped to it.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The scenario's human-readable title, shown after its name in the heading of its sequence diagram (`sd {name} — {title}`). When empty, the heading is the name alone.

fields.name: steps
fields.description: The steps of the scenario, in order. Must not be empty and must be an ordered subsequence of the referenced task's runnables.

element_kinds.description: One step of a sequence scenario: the runnable it shows, its component named by exactly one of `swc` and `instance`, with an optional note. The `(swc, instance, runnable)` triple, the absent selector as `null`, is the step's identity; the step must be mapped to the scenario's task, and a step written the same way appears at most once per scenario.

fields.name: swc
fields.description: The name of the declared software component the step runs in; exactly one of `swc` and `instance` is set. Part of the step's composite identity, and so immutable.

fields.name: instance
fields.description: The occurrence of a component below the root composition the step runs in, as a `/`-joined path of composition member names from the root composition down — a member of the root is its member name alone, a nested one `outer/inner` — never starting with the root composition's own name; exactly one of `swc` and `instance` is set. Part of the step's composite identity, and so immutable.

fields.name: runnable
fields.description: The name of a runnable of that component, which must be mapped to the scenario's task. Part of the composite identity, and so immutable.

fields.name: note
fields.description: Free text shown beside the step on its sequence diagram; when non-empty the step's activation is labelled `{runnable} — {note}`.

expected.notes: The same document the default form answers with `description` restored on the layer, on every kind and on every field that declares one, and with the three descriptor booleans spelled out where the default form omits them at `false` — `optional` on the layer, `required` and `immutable` on every field. Nothing else is restored, because nothing else is left out. `baseline` is the stand-in token every vector carries; a harness replaces it with the project's own.
